audit.whatIsWrong: win[6] reads Pantheon while the late paragraph opens 'This is Vlad's game and you know it' and whys[6] says 'He out-scales hard'.
audit.why: Two strings in the entry, a 49.57% win rate over 1523 games, and the packet's levelChart for this pairing all give the two-item stage to Vladimir.
audit.corrected: content win[6] moved from Pantheon to Vladimir.

audit.whatIsWrong: Sanguine Pool's 'long cooldown' is referenced five times and never once given a number, and the pool's duration is never stated either.
audit.why: Sanguine Pool is 28/25/22/19/16s and it makes him untargetable for 2 seconds. Both numbers are decisive: 28 seconds at rank 1 is the longest defensive cooldown you will face in a top lane, and 2 seconds is exactly how long you have to not be spending your combo. Transfusion is 9s at rank 1 and Hemoplague 120s.
audit.corrected: Written into early, mid, whys[2], whys[3], whys[4], spikes[1], spikes[2], wants.you[0], wants.you[1], wants.foe[0], breakdown.cooldowns, dosFull[0] and report[5].

audit.whatIsWrong: Tides of Blood is described only as 'his E poke' and the entry advises blocking it with Aegis Assault.
audit.why: Riot: 'Vladimir pays his own health to charge up a reservoir of blood which, when released, deals damage in the area around him but can be blocked by enemy units.' Two facts the page never uses — his poke costs him health, and it is stopped by units, so standing behind a minion denies it outright. That is far better advice than spending a 22-second channel on it.
audit.corrected: Minion-block written into early; the self-health cost into early and phases[0].why.

audit.why: Nothing in Vladimir's kit text describes percent maximum health damage. What does explain his scaling is Crimson Pact: every 30 bonus health gives him 1 ability power and every 1 ability power gives 1.6 bonus health. That is the real reason Rylai's and Riftmaker make him unkillable, and it was never mentioned.
audit.corrected: Percent-health claim replaced with Crimson Pact's conversion in whys[5], whys[6], spikes[3] and late.

audit.whatIsWrong: Hemoplague is never named and its damage amplification is never mentioned.
audit.why: Riot: affected enemies take increased damage for the duration, and it heals him for each champion hit. Standing in the plague makes every subsequent trade worse, which is the actual reason not to fight in it.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Passive shield + Q poke wins level 1 outright'.
audit.why: Pantheon's passive is Mortal Will; Vladimir's passive is Crimson Pact, which the entry also never names.

edits.before: Vlad is one of the weakest level 1s in the game and so are you — but you spike harder and faster. edits.before: Through 4-5 you still control the lane with empowered-Q poke and E blocks, but Vlad stabilizes — his Q drain heals your chip and he just farms. notes: This entry says 'the long cooldown' or 'the pool's long cooldown' five times without ever printing a number, in a matchup that is entirely about one cooldown. Sanguine Pool is 28 seconds at rank 1 and makes him untargetable for 2 seconds. Those two figures turn every piece of advice here into something a player can actually count, and 28 seconds is long enough that baiting it genuinely wins the lane. Two facts about Tides of Blood were also missing and both are useful: it costs Vladimir his own health to charge, and Riot's text says it 'can be blocked by enemy units' — so standing behind a minion denies his poke entirely, which is better than spending a 22-second Aegis Assault on it. Removed the claim that his drain is percent maximum health; nothing in his kit text supports it. What does explain his scaling is Crimson Pact, never named in the entry: 30 bonus health gives 1 AP and 1 AP gives 1.6 health, which is precisely why Rylai's and Riftmaker make him unkillable.
